decisions.quote: The well‐known study by Leiponen and Helfat (2010) examined how firms increased their odds of innovation success by pursuing multiple parallel innovation objectives and knowledge sources. We replicate their study across geographic and temporal contexts using three sets of data: from Finland ( N = 884) in 2006–2008 and from other European countries in two different time periods ( N = 36,480 in 2006–2008 and 24,326 in 2008–2010).
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists for this work. The source title and abstract explicitly state that the paper is a quasi-replication of Leiponen and Helfat (2010) examining how firms increase innovation success through the breadth of parallel innovation objectives and knowledge sources, diminishing returns to breadth, and the interaction between knowledge sources and innovation objectives. Crossref metadata in bibliography_metadata.json for shipped row input_row_index 961 (doi_o: 10.1002/smj.807) confirms that this is the exact same article by Aija Leiponen and Constance E. Helfat, titled 'Innovation objectives, knowledge sources, and the benefits of breadth' in Strategic Management Journal, Vol. 31, Issue 2, pp. 224-236. The year discrepancy between shipped row 961 (year_o: 2009) and the blind target (year: 2010, with title left empty because only the abstract was available) arises solely because 10.1002/smj.807 was published online on September 22, 2009 and in print in Volume 31, Issue 2 in 2010. Thus target_index 0 is already represented by shipped input_row_index 961.
